TDD Kata: Car Dealership Inventory System 

Objective 

The goal of this kata is to design, build, and test a full-stack Car Dealership Inventory System. This project will test your skills in API development, database management, frontend implementation, testing, and modern development workflows, including the use of AI tools. 

Core Requirements 

1. Backend API (RESTful) 

You are to build a robust backend API that will serve as the brain of the application. 

Technology: Choose one of the following: Node.js/TypeScript (with Express/NestJS), Python (with Django/FastAPI), or Ruby (with Rails). 

Database: The application must connect to a database (e.g., PostgreSQL, MongoDB, SQLite). An in-memory database is not sufficient. 

User Authentication: 

Users must be able to register and log in. 

Implement token-based authentication (e.g., JWT) to secure certain API endpoints. 

API Endpoints: 

Auth: POST /api/auth/register, POST /api/auth/login 

Vehicles (Protected): 

POST /api/vehicles: Add a new vehicle. 

GET /api/vehicles: View a list of all available vehicles. 

GET /api/vehicles/search: Search for vehicles by make, model, category, or price range. 

PUT /api/vehicles/:id: Update a vehicle's details. 

DELETE /api/vehicles/:id: Delete a vehicle (Admin only). 

Inventory (Protected): 

POST /api/vehicles/:id/purchase: Purchase a vehicle, decreasing its quantity. 

POST /api/vehicles/:id/restock: Restock a vehicle, increasing its quantity (Admin only). 

Each vehicle must have a unique ID, make, model, category, price, and quantity in stock. 

2. Frontend Application 

You must build a modern, single-page application (SPA) to interact with your backend API. 

Technology: You must use HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind, and React 

Functionality: 

User registration and login forms. 

A dashboard or homepage to display all available vehicles. 

Functionality to search and filter vehicles. 

A "Purchase" button on each vehicle, which should be disabled if the quantity is zero. 

(For Admin Users) Forms/UI to add, update, and delete vehicles. 

Design: This is a chance to show your creativity. The application should be visually appealing, responsive, and provide a great user experience. 

Process & Technical Guidelines 

1. Test-Driven Development (TDD) 

Write tests before implementing functionality. We expect to see a clear "Red-Green-Refactor" pattern in your commit history, especially for the backend logic. Aim for high test coverage with meaningful test cases. 

2. Clean Coding Practices 

Write clean, readable, and maintainable code. Follow SOLID principles and other best practices in software design. Your code should be well-documented with meaningful comments and clear naming conventions. 

3. Git & Version Control 

Use Git for version control. Commit your changes frequently with clear, descriptive messages that narrate your development journey. 

4. AI Usage Policy (Important) 

We believe AI is a critical tool in the modern software development lifecycle. You are encouraged and expected to use AI tools. However, you must be transparent about it. 

AI Co-authorship: For every commit where you used an AI tool (for generating boilerplate, writing tests, debugging, etc.), you must add the AI as a co-author. 

How to add a co-author: At the end of your commit message, add two empty lines, followed by the co-author trailer. 

git commit -m "feat: Implement user registration endpoint 
 
Used an AI assistant to generate the initial boilerplate for the 
controller and service, then manually added validation logic. 
 
Co-authored-by: AI Tool Name <AI@users.noreply.github.com>" 

README Documentation: Your README.md file must include a detailed section titled "My AI Usage". In this section, you must describe: 

Which AI tools you used (e.g., GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.). 

How you used them (e.g., "I used Gemini to brainstorm API endpoint structures," or "I asked Copilot to generate unit tests for my service layer"). 

Your reflection on how AI impacted your workflow. 

Interview Discussion: Be prepared to discuss your AI usage in detail during the interview. We are interested in how you leverage these tools effectively and responsibly. 

Deliverables 

A public Git repository link (e.g., on GitHub, GitLab). 

A comprehensive README.md file that includes: 

A clear explanation of the project. 

Detailed instructions on how to set up and run the project locally (both backend and frontend). 

Screenshots of your final application in action. 

The mandatory "My AI Usage" section. 

A test report showing the results of your test suite. 

A root PROMPTS.md containing your raw, unedited AI chat logs or public chat links (no AI-generated summaries). 

(Optional - Brownie Points) A link to the deployed, live application on a platform like Vercel, Netlify, Heroku, or AWS. 

Note: Plagiarism is strictly forbidden. While we encourage AI assistance, submitting code copied from other repositories or developers will result in immediate rejection. We want to see your work, augmented by modern tools.

function grid() {
  let s = '';
  for (let x = 40; x < 800; x += 40) s += `<line x1="${x}" y1="0" x2="${x}" y2="450"/>`;
  for (let y = 30; y < 450; y += 40) s += `<line x1="0" y1="${y}" x2="800" y2="${y}"/>`;
  return s;
}

function wheel(x, y, r, accent) {
  return `
    <circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="${r}" fill="#07070f" stroke="#1e293b" stroke-width="7"/>
    <circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="${r * 0.55}" fill="#0f172a" stroke="${accent}" stroke-opacity="0.5" stroke-width="2"/>
    <circle cx="${x}" cy="${y}" r="${r * 0.22}" fill="${accent}" fill-opacity="0.35"/>`;
}

  const wy = 318;

      <stop offset="0" stop-color="${car.body}"/>
      <stop offset="0.55" stop-color="${car.body2}"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#0b0b16"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <linearGradient id="window" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="#c7d2fe" stop-opacity="0.55"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="#1e1b4b" stop-opacity="0.9"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="glow">
      <stop offset="0" stop-color="${car.body}" stop-opacity="0.45"/>
      <stop offset="1" stop-color="${car.body}" stop-opacity="0"/>
    </radialGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect width="800" height="450" fill="url(#bg)"/>
  <g opacity="0.13" stroke="#6366f1" stroke-width="1">${grid()}</g>
  <circle cx="400" cy="235" r="245" fill="url(#glow)"/>
  <ellipse cx="400" cy="352" rx="292" ry="26" fill="#000000" opacity="0.55"/>
  <path d="${car.bodyPath}" fill="url(#body)" stroke="${car.accent}" stroke-opacity="0.55" stroke-width="2.5"/>
  ${car.windows}
  <path d="${car.line}" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-opacity="0.2" stroke-width="2"/>
  <path d="M${car.wheels[0] + 52} 300 L${car.wheels[1] - 52} 300" stroke="#000" stroke-opacity="0.25" stroke-width="3"/>
  <rect x="${car.wheels[1] + 82}" y="282" width="26" height="10" rx="5" fill="${car.accent}" fill-opacity="0.85"/>
  <rect x="126" y="284" width="22" height="9" rx="4" fill="#ef4444" fill-opacity="0.8"/>
  ${car.lightBar ? `<rect x="330" y="288" width="140" height="5" rx="2.5" fill="${car.accent}" fill-opacity="0.9"/>` : ''}
  ${wheel(car.wheels[0], wy, wr, car.accent)}
  ${wheel(car.wheels[1], wy, wr, car.accent)}
</svg>
`;
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, `${name}.svg`), svg, 'utf8');
}
console.log('Generated', Object.keys(cars).length, 'car illustrations.');

import json, os, sqlite3, shutil

ROOT = r"C:\Users\anups\Desktop\TDD Kata Car Dealership Inventory System"
ANTI = r"C:\Users\anups\.gemini\antigravity-ide\brain\18ce1bbe-0956-4fc0-b020-ede49dfed80d\.system_generated\logs\transcript_full.jsonl"
OC_DB = os.path.expanduser('~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db')
OC_SID = 'ses_e8c4ddc46ffeqVQHEnrHcFGlll'
LOG_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, 'docs', 'ai-logs')
os.makedirs(LOG_DIR, exist_ok=True)

shutil.copyfile(ANTI, os.path.join(LOG_DIR, 'antigravity-transcript.jsonl'))

# Export the completion session as raw JSONL too.
conn = sqlite3.connect(OC_DB)
rows = conn.execute(
    "select id, type, seq, time_created, time_updated, data from session_message where session_id=? order by seq",
    (OC_SID,),
).fetchall()
with open(os.path.join(LOG_DIR, 'opencode-session.jsonl'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    for id_, typ, seq, tc, tu, data in rows:
        f.write(json.dumps({
            'id': id_, 'type': typ, 'seq': seq,
            'time_created': tc, 'time_updated': tu,
            'data': json.loads(data),
        }, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n')

out = []
out.append('# PROMPTS.md — Raw AI Session Logs\n')
out.append('This file contains the raw prompts and responses from the two AI sessions used to build this project. '
           'The original JSONL exports are committed alongside this file under `docs/ai-logs/`.\n')
out.append('- `docs/ai-logs/antigravity-transcript.jsonl` — original build session (Antigravity IDE / Claude Sonnet 4.6 Thinking)\n'
           '- `docs/ai-logs/opencode-session.jsonl` — completion and verification session (OpenCode / DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Free)\n')
out.append('Only Markdown headings and code fences were added for readability. Prompt and response text is otherwise unedited.\n')

# ── Session 1 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
out.append('\n---\n\n## Session 1 — Original build (Antigravity IDE)\n')
out.append('Source: `transcript_full.jsonl` from the Antigravity brain directory. '
           'System bookkeeping entries and tool output bodies are omitted from this readable view; '
           'the complete raw file is included in `docs/ai-logs/`.\n')

with open(ANTI, encoding='utf-8') as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        r = json.loads(line)
        typ = r.get('type')
        step = r.get('step_index')
        created = r.get('created_at', '')
        if typ == 'USER_INPUT':
            out.append(f'\n### Step {step} — User ({created})\n\n~~~~text\n{r.get("content", "")}\n~~~~\n')
        elif typ == 'ASK_QUESTION':
            out.append(f'\n### Step {step} — User answers\n\n~~~~text\n{r.get("content", "")}\n~~~~\n')
        elif typ == 'PLANNER_RESPONSE':
            content = r.get('content')
            thinking = r.get('thinking')
            calls = r.get('tool_calls')
            if not (content or thinking or calls):
                continue
            out.append(f'\n### Step {step} — Assistant\n')
            if content:
                out.append(f'\n~~~~text\n{content}\n~~~~\n')
            if thinking:
                out.append(f'\n<details><summary>Model thinking</summary>\n\n~~~~text\n{thinking}\n~~~~\n\n</details>\n')
            if calls:
                out.append('\n**Tool calls:**\n\n~~~~json\n' + json.dumps(calls, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n~~~~\n')

# ── Session 2 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
out.append('\n---\n\n## Session 2 — Completion and verification (OpenCode)\n')
out.append('Source: `opencode-session.jsonl`, exported from the OpenCode session database. '
           'Assistant reasoning and full tool output bodies are omitted from this readable view; '
           'the complete raw file is included in `docs/ai-logs/`.\n')

for id_, typ, seq, tc, tu, data in rows:
    d = json.loads(data)
    if typ == 'user':
        text = d.get('text') or d.get('metadata', {}).get('displayText', '')
        out.append(f'\n### Seq {seq} — User\n\n~~~~text\n{text}\n~~~~\n')
    elif typ == 'assistant':
        out.append(f'\n### Seq {seq} — Assistant\n')
        for part in d.get('content', []):
            ptype = part.get('type')
            if ptype == 'text' and part.get('text'):
                out.append(f'\n~~~~text\n{part["text"]}\n~~~~\n')
            elif ptype == 'tool':
                name = part.get('name')
                inp = part.get('state', {}).get('input', {})
                out.append(f'\n**Tool call — `{name}`**\n\n~~~~json\n{json.dumps(inp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)}\n~~~~\n')

with open(os.path.join(ROOT, 'PROMPTS.md'), 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write('\n'.join(out))
print('Wrote PROMPTS.md and raw logs.')
